summary: S'STACK helps Gabonese farmers — mostly women growing cassava — decide when to plant as rainfall patterns shift. It turns NASA POWER satellite-derived data (rainfall, temperature, root-zone soil moisture and long-term climate normals) into a simple sowing verdict: favorable, risky or unfavorable. Farmers get advice on a web app or by sending a voice message to a Telegram bot, in plain French. The code computes every number from NASA data; an AI assistant only explains it. This matters because most Gabonese food-crop farmers rely on rain-fed agriculture and still plan by memory of seasons that no longer behave as before.
details:
What it does

- Detects the start of the rainy season from NASA POWER daily rainfall (rule: at least 20 mm over 3 days, with no 7-day dry spell in the following 20 days).

- Compares the last 7 and 30 days of rain with NASA climatological normals ("40% drier than usual").

- Reads root-zone soil moisture (GWETROOT) to classify soil as dry, adequate or wet.

- Combines these indicators into a sowing verdict and a short action.

- Covers 8 sites across Gabon (Tchibanga, Mouila, Lambaréné, Libreville, Oyem, Makokou, Koulamoutou, Franceville) and any GPS point.

How farmers use it

- Web app: dashboard with verdict, indicators, 30-day charts and a map.

- Telegram bot: farmers send a voice note; speech is transcribed, the agent answers with the local NASA data sheet.

- AI assistant "Mbolo": answers questions using a data sheet built by our code, with guardrails so it never invents figures.

How it works

- Back-end: TypeScript, Hono, Zod validation, caching of NASA calls.

- Front-end: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, Recharts.

- AI: Groq (Llama models) with Gemini fallback; Whisper for speech-to-text.

- Database/auth: Supabase. No personal data of farmers is shared.

Why it matters

In Gabon, women make up 64.3% of farm holders (2019 Agricultural Census, results 2021) and cassava covers 72.78% of food-crop plots (EPVA survey 2022, published 2023). S'STACK gives them a climate-aware planting calendar from free NASA data, on the phone they already own.

Next steps

Field testing with producers in the Nyanga and Ngounié provinces, local-language voice, and SMS access for basic phones.
dataRefs: NASA POWER Daily API (PRECTOTCORR, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, GWETROOT)\t
